decisions.reason: Although technologically related to advanced packaging, its disappearance from the website after 2019 suggests the market test revealed limited traction, so we would reallocate effort to stronger core wafer offerings.
This carrier wafer is very close to the core carrier and thin-wafer handling business and is likely inexpensive to maintain as a niche option, so we would keep it available.

The Cu-interposer glass wafer was a more development-intensive packaging option with no visible follow-through after launch, implying uncertainty has resolved unfavorably relative to its support cost.

As a separate off-the-shelf brand, it is easy to reverse and its one-year visibility suggests the channel did not justify ongoing marketing complexity, even if the underlying standard wafers remain in the core business.

Glass-based circuit boards are distant from the firm's core substrate business and, after only brief visibility, should be abandoned to free resources for nearer-term semiconductor wafer opportunities.
